newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower, new low set in March.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower, new low set in March.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mostly lower, led by March, with a new contract low of $3.54-1/2 per bushel set in that month on persistent reminders of adequate supplies of wheat worldwide, traders said.
The previous low for March was $3.56 and was set Wednesday.

"There was a lot of spread trading in the March/May and March/July," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures. "A lot of people were getting their house in order before deliveries and the world supply hit it."
Wheat remains bearish with only light commercial buying.
The commercials are going after wheat only on an "as needed" basis, they said.

Traders virtually shrugged off overnight business for U.S. wheat including news a Philippine firm bought 40,000 tonnes and news Lebanon invited tenders to buy 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat. Also in the background was an Iraqi tender for wheat but many in the market do not believe Iraq will buy from the U.S.
Wheat closed three cents per bushel lower to 1/2 higher, with March down two at $3.56. May settled up 1/2 at $3.51-3/4 and July was down 1/2 at $3.39.
The market was positioning before first notice day for deliveries on the March contract slated for February 28.

Some trade sources indicated the jury apparently is still out on whether Egypt this week bought U.S. or Australian wheat. A spokeswoman for the Australian Wheat Board said Friday that the sourcing had not yet been confirmed for Egypt's purchase of 110,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian wheat. There was talk Thursday the wheat would almost certainly be purchased from the U.S.
The wheat market took note of news Friday the French cereals authority ONIC planned to hike its estimate for French soft wheat exports to non-EU countries by 250,000 tonnes.
Also a key bullish input for the new crop July contract, especially in the KCBT market, disappeared late this week.
The market recently was becoming cognizant of dry weather in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region but snowfall near midweek took the sting out of that potential supply reducer.
A winter storm, now moving out of Kansas into Missouri, left a crop-enhancing seven-inch (18 cm) blanket of snow in some areas of Kansas, meteorologists said.

Chartists pointed to a near term oversold scenario for the March contract with the nine day relative strength index (RSI) closing at 26-1/2 percent. Technicians consider an RSI of 30 or less as a barometer of an oversold market. They cited bearish flags for the March through July contract from the four and 20-day moving averages.
Early Friday, first support in the March was pegged at $3.55 and second support at $3.46-1/2. The session low for March was $3.54-1/2, the contract low.
Prudential Securities sold roughly two million bushels each of the March and July and Dean Witter sold one million bushels of March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, below the 13,309 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, ING Derivatives bought 250 July $3.50 calls at 12 cents and Term Commodities sold 200 March $3.60 calls at four cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,500 contracts, below the 6,738 traded Thursday.
